result.title: Retraining-Free Depth Pruning of Vision Transformers: A Cross Domain Study of Layer Redundancy
result.summary: Transformer architectures have achieved strong results in natural language processing and computer vision, but their deployment is limited by high computational, memory and storage costs, motivating research into model compression techniques, such as pruning, while preserving performance. Prior work has shown substantial redundancy in large language models (LLMs), and redundancy in vision transformers has also been investigated, but it remains less systematically analyzed than in LLMs. In this work, we extend similarity-based redundancy analysis to vision models by measuring cosine similarity between layer inputs and outputs to identify transformations with minimal impact. We study redundancy patterns across several transformer architectures and find that deep vision transformers such as DINOv2 and SwinV2, like language models, exhibit significant redundancy. We then evaluate how this redundancy can be exploited to improve efficiency, analyzing the trade-off between inference speed and performance degradation under different pruning strategies. Our results show that moderate pruning can yield substantial acceleration with limited impact on accuracy, and that 20% of the DINOv2 blocks can be removed without any retraining, for a 1.24x throughput gain and a 20% lower energy per image at a relative accuracy loss below 1% on ImageNet-1K. We further propose a model selection pipeline that automatically identifies the best pruned configuration for a given dataset, reducing FLOPs by 13% to 27% on average across architectures with an average accuracy change between -0.3 and +1.0 points.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文将基于相似度的冗余分析扩展到视觉 Transformer：用层输入与输出的余弦相似度衡量各层变换的影响，在 DINOv2、SwinV2 等模型上做免重训练的深度剪枝，并给出自动选择剪枝配置的流程，报告精度与效率的折中。
AI.relevance_reason: 其逐层 latent 相似度度量正是「相似度受深度与层位置影响」的具体线索，可供核查哪些层的内部状态变化最小、视觉必要信息集中在何处；但该工作目标为分类模型的压缩效率，与推理期状态生成无直接关系，迁移需自行判断。
